clue.text: Perhaps stole a penny in church

indicators.note: the letters for 'a penny' are placed inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone may have pinched a coin while at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as the verb of theft; here it is a shoulder wrap, and 'Perhaps' says the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is one kind of shoulder covering, a cloak-like garment worn over the upper body.

clue.text: Cutters — sailing vessels

definitions.meaning: tools that clip or trim, such as for hair or hedges

explanation.definitionFit: Shears for trimming are one sense; fast tea-trade sailing ships are the other.

clue.text: Reported butcher's offence

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: butcher's hook is rhyming slang for a look, a peek

explanation.surface: A meat seller is said to have committed a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a 'butcher's' (from 'butcher's hook') is a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence is a fit of resentment or wounded pride.

clue.text: European doctor managed to cut this writer's skin

indicators.note: the European doctor who managed is set to slice into the words for this writer

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as ME
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
ran a business means managed it

explanation.surface: A continental medic operated on the setter's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin sheet of tissue lining or covering an organ is a skin in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Clear I've got over depression

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters of I've are turned over, read upwards

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Someone says plainly they have recovered from feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests a low mood, but it is a hollow; 'got over' sounds like recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious or plain to see, as in 'it was clear that'.

clue.text: Go under bed and grin wickedly — it's where mating takes place

indicators.note: the letters behave badly and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cheeky invitation to dive under the covers and leer naughtily.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where animals reproduce, such as a nesting site for birds.

clue.text: Change the last word daughter expressed, heartlessly

parts.note: amen is said at the very end of a prayer

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for expressed is removed

parts.note: meant, as in what someone meant to say

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted daughter's final remark brings about a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision or alteration to a text or law is a change.

clue.text: Gossiper seldom bites tongue

indicators.note: the two words have their teeth in the letters within them

explanation.surface: A chatterbox rarely holds back their words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bites tongue' looks like an idiom for staying quiet; 'tongue' is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland is a tongue, meaning a language.

clue.text: Prejudiced Conservative supporting Germany is almost deplorable

indicators.note: in a down clue the Conservative goes underneath, holding up the rest

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for deplorable is left off

parts.note: criminal, as in 'a criminal waste'
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A biased right-wing backer of Germany is nearly appalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfairly treating people differently because of race, sex and so on is being biased.

clue.text: Nice Bordeaux? Mentions swallowing one

indicators.note: the word for mentions takes in the letter for one

parts.note: to cite is to mention or quote
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone praises a pleasant French wine while drinking one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective and 'Bordeaux' the wine; both are French towns, the question mark showing they are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and Bordeaux are both examples of large French towns.

clue.text: Curiosity in queen's visit is spreading

indicators.note: the letters of these four words spread out and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nosiness is growing about a royal visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Curiosity and nosiness are synonyms: a strong desire to know about things.

clue.text: Specify page concerning writer

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An instruction to name the page about an author.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down or stipulate a requirement is to specify it, as a doctor does a treatment.

clue.text: Be good enough to hold strange, tailless bird

indicators.note: the word for being good enough wraps around the shortened word for strange

parts.note: 'that will do' means that is good enough

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for strange is cut off

parts.note: odd means strange

explanation.surface: A request to look after an odd bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless pigeon of Mauritius is a famous bird.

clue.text: Continues to be stiff?

definitions.meaning: a stiff is slang for a corpse, and a body is a person's mortal leftovers

explanation.definitionFit: Stays the same is one sense; the other is a dead body, slang 'stiff', with the question mark flagging the slang.

clue.text: Hindu instructor — mother cut his hair

parts.note: MA is a word for mother

indicators.note: the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A guru's mother gave him a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu sage or spiritual teacher, a guru, bears this title.

clue.text: Kind nurse — the woman leaving hospital

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them

indicators.note: the letter for hospital departs from the word for the woman

parts.note: her is a word for the woman

explanation.surface: A caring nurse is described as she goes off from her ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle and caring: a kind person is soft-hearted and compassionate.

clue.text: The lady's surrounded by deer most savage

indicators.note: the lady's word sits inside the word for deer

parts.note: a hart is a male red deer
she's is a contraction of the lady is

explanation.surface: A woman finds herself ringed by vicious stags.
explanation.definitionFit: Most severe or cruel is the superlative of savage in its harsh sense.

clue.text: Quiet beer knocked back entertaining one Australian woman

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the reversed beer word takes in the letter for one, as a host has a guest
the beer word is read backwards, as a drink is downed

parts.note: ale is a beer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drink is downed quietly while a woman from Down Under is being entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns ALE into ELA, and 'entertaining' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a girl or female is this word.

clue.text: It shows level of current temperature after girl turns up on English river

indicators.note: the temperature letter comes after the girl
in a down clue being on something means sitting above it
in a down clue the girl's name is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A gauge of water flow reads warm when a girl arrives by an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' and 'river' suggest water; the current here is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument measuring electric current in amperes is a meter for amps.

clue.text: Meet with sailors, for example, at rear of port, welcomed by Rear Admiral

indicators.note: the inner pieces are taken in by the letters for the senior naval rank
the final letter of port is used

explanation.surface: Sailors gathered at the back of a harbour are greeted by a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boating race event is a meeting, or meet, of crews in sailing boats or rowing boats.

clue.text: Government starts to regret electing good-for-nothing — time to remove leader

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken
the first letter of the word time is taken off

parts.note: taken as the word time itself

explanation.surface: Voters begin to rue choosing a useless candidate, and it's time to oust the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling system or administration, especially an authoritarian one, is a government.

clue.text: Sailor carefully nets whale

indicators.note: the two words catch the letters within them, as a net catches fish

explanation.surface: A seaman cautiously catches a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a large black and white toothed cetacean.

clue.text: Animals go off trees

indicators.note: the letters go off, bad or awry, and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wildlife departs from the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowering shrubs and trees with large showy blooms, named after the botanist Magnol.

clue.text: Dialect I'd picked up in Isle of Man

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the island's abbreviation
in a down clue the letters of I'd are lifted, read upwards

explanation.surface: A speaker says they learnt the local speech on the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like learning; it is the upward reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of expression peculiar to a language or region, so a local way of speaking.

clue.text: Slight lifting for buttocks

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is raised, read upwards

parts.note: to snub someone is to slight them

explanation.surface: A small lift for the bottom, like a cosmetic procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective; it is the verb, an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the bottom, from the rounded bread rolls.

clue.text: Dirty mask until person's changed

indicators.note: the letters of these words are altered, the 's reading as 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a grimy face covering on until they have swapped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person's changed' reads 'person has changed', so the 's is not part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty play in sport is unfair, against the code of good sportsmanship.

clue.text: Craft I spy had first of repairs here?

definitions.text: Craft I spy had first of repairs here?

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion or shape, so these letters are reworked
the opening letter of repairs is used

explanation.surface: A boat I saw got its first repairs at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like the boat but it is the anagram signal for ISPYHAD plus R; the whole clue then describes a place where vessels are fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where ships are built and mended is where a vessel would get its repairs.

clue.text: Obscene stuff saint found in Greek letter? On the contrary

indicators.note: this says one piece sits inside another
reverses the stated order, so the Greek letter goes inside the saint rather than the other way round

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Filth involving a holy figure turns up in a Greek text.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or pornographic material is obscene stuff, as in a filthy picture.
